newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-JORDAN PLAYS DOWN THREAT OF PROST.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-JORDAN PLAYS DOWN THREAT OF PROST.

text.p: Team chief Eddie Jordan found the official launch of his 1997 challenge overshadowed on Thursday by speculation that Frenchman Alain Prost is poised to form his own Grand Prix team.

According to the latest wave of rumours in Formula One, it is understood that Prost - who is expected to announce next month that he has bought the Ligier team - will take over Jordan's supply of Peugeot engines.
But Jordan, one of the most colourful team owners in Formula One, played down the rumours about any threat to his team when he spoke at the unveiling.

Jordan, whose cars are powered by the same Peugeot engines linked with Prost's effort - which is not expected to begin racing until 1998 -- admitted that this was the final year of his own three-year deal with the French manufacturer.
But, he said, he was not worried about the future.
"This is the third year of our three-year contract and we have never been closer," said Jordan.

"We are working for the same aim and the improvement of our team is a major step forward. All the talk about the future is not for today and the resilience of Jordan and Peugeot has never been stronger."
Peugeot's sporting director Pierre-Michel Fauconnier acknowledged the rumours about Peugeot's links with Prost's team, but when asked about it would only say: "I am afraid I cannot comment."
Jordan's new car was notable for its revised aerodynamic package and many innovative design features. The team believe these should see the car lap up to two seconds faster than last year's machine.

"The difference is black and white," said the designer, Gary Anderson. "That is down to the investment the team has put in the future and our computer simulations show that at Silverstone we should be between 1.7 and 1.8 seconds faster than last year. I believe it will happen."
The team's two drivers, Italian Giancarlo Fisichella and German Ralf Schumacher, were introduced by Jordan as the "youngest and most talented couple in Formula One" and both stressed their ambitions.

Fisichella said: "My eight grands prix with Minardi were important for experience, but they were very difficult. This year, I am racing with a competitive team, I am grateful for the people and I want to give the team a podium or possible victory."
Schumacher, the brother of double world champion Michael, said there was more pressure on him because of his name but he hoped to be able to concentrate on racing.
"Michael has had six years in Formula One and I have had a very quick and straight line into Grand Prix racing. I speak to him quite often.
"He says don't expect to do too much because at the end of the year we will sit down together and see what the season brought us."
The new car will be given its first run at Silverstone on Monday before going to Spain for testing at Jerez in advance of the opening race in Melbourne on March 9.
